**Needs changes before merge.**

Reviewed head `dbe37ad2c` (the delta commit `give each thread its own temp file name` was read on top of `f5d99934d`). Trial-merged with main `ef1572114` as local commit `bc9e8e2a`; the merge is clean.

## What looks good

- `project::save` now writes through `machine::store::write_atomic`: a temp file in the same folder, `write_all`, `sync_all`, then `rename` over the target. `crates/app/src/machine/store.rs:127-152`. The temp file is in the target's own folder, so the rename is never across filesystems.
- On any error from create, write, sync or rename, the temp file is removed and the target is not touched (`store.rs:145-148`). The old project stays byte for byte.
- The write is `sync_all`ed before the rename. A power loss after the rename can keep the old file; it cannot leave a part-written project. This matches the decision doc.
- The two refusals of the old plain write are kept: a missing folder (`crates/app/src/project/wire.rs:319`) and a read-only file (`wire.rs:322`).
- The temp name now carries the process ID and a per-thread number (`store.rs:107-121`), so two saves of one file on two threads, or in two processes, never share a temp file. `thread_number` takes one number from one `AtomicUsize` per thread; no `unwrap`, `expect` or panic.
- The saved text, the file format and `PROJECT_VERSION` do not change. `save_text` (the browser path) is untouched.
- The new tests sit in `crates/app/tests/`, which is the crate that defines `project::save` and `machine::store`.

## Results merged with main (locally, this machine)

Trial merge `bc9e8e2a` = main `ef1572114` + PR head `dbe37ad2c`, clean.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green, 8 of 8 steps, 0 failed.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| app build (`--no-run`) | ok |
| app lib | ok, 297 passed |
| contour_dxf_sketch | ok, 4 passed |
| import_step_open_shell | ok, 4 passed |
| machine_edit | ok, 13 passed (incl. `two_threads_never_share_a_temp_file`) |
| model_solid_ranges | ok, 4 passed |
| project_roundtrip | ok, 80 passed (incl. the 4 new atomic-save tests) |
| sketch_project | ok, 14 passed |

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean, exit 0.

One note on the run: step 01 first failed on a missing `solidcore` object file. That was a stale artifact from a gate run I stopped when the head moved, not the PR. I cleared `target/debug/build/solidcore-*` and re-ran; the clean run above is the result.

## Heavy lanes

The diff changes `crates/app/src`, so it reaches every `app` heavy target (207 lanes via `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run --base origin/main`). The PR body says these are not run yet. This review ran `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main` on this head:

Not run to completion by this review. A local run reached lane 133 of 207 with no failure when this review was written, and it was still running. Per the review laws, a reached heavy lane that is not run is a blocker. Not a pass. The author must run `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main` to green on this head before the PR is flagged ready, and the PR body must name the lanes that ran. The PR body says they are not run yet.

## Requested before merge

1. `crates/app/src/project/wire.rs:322` - the read-only check misses a file you cannot write but whose mode has a write bit. `Permissions::readonly()` on Unix is true only when every write bit is clear (`mode & 0o222 == 0`). A `.camproj` owned by another user with mode `0644` in a group-writable shared folder is not "readonly", so the save runs. The rename then replaces that file, because `rename(2)` needs write permission on the folder, not on the file. The old `std::fs::write` opened the file for writing and failed with `EACCES`, so it kept the file. Failure scenario: `/shared/job.camproj` is owned by alice, mode `0644`; the folder is group-writable; bob saves from CamCraft; alice's project is replaced by bob's project. This is the shared-folder case that #3509 names. Fix: when the target exists, test writability the way the old write did, for example `std::fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).open(path)` (no `truncate`), and refuse on error with the "is read-only" message. That check follows the effective user and group and keeps the friendly text.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- `crates/app/tests/project_roundtrip.rs` is 5574 lines and grows by 74. The 400-line rule flags growth of a file already over, not a blocker; a later split along a domain seam would help.
- A writable project file inside a folder you cannot write now fails to save: the temp file cannot be created, so `write_project` returns an error. The old plain write succeeded (it needs no folder write permission). This is a safe refusal and the old file stays, but it is a behavior change not in the decision doc.
- A project path that is a symbolic link is replaced by a plain file; the link's target keeps the old content (`docs/decisions/3509-atomic-project-save.md`, "Known limits"). It is documented, so not a blocker, but a user on a shared folder with a linked project will not see the target updated.
- The failed-save test injects the fault with a folder in the temp file's place. That exercises the `File::create` failure, not a `write_all` that stops at a full disk. The code path is the same closure and any error removes the temp, but the mid-write failure is not directly pinned.
- The PR body ends with `Effort: low`; issue #3509 carries `effort:high`, and the safety floor puts data-saving work at high. The body line should match or be dropped.
- The PR is still a draft. The four pinning tests: `a_failed_project_save_keeps_the_old_file` and the two refusal tests would be red on the base code (the old write succeeds, or the message differs); `a_project_save_replaces_the_file_and_leaves_no_temp_file` passes on the base code and guards against a new temp leak; `two_threads_never_share_a_temp_file` was red before the delta commit.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: eab5f1932ca003145b6a6d42e14e3b44e4696a63 -->

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Re-review of the fix for the one blocker of the review at `dbe37ad2c`. I read the delta commit `eab5f1932` and the tests it adds. I trial-merged the head with main `64b737729` and ran the tests locally.

## What looks good

- The write probe is correct. `write_project` opens an existing target with `OpenOptions::new().write(true).open(path)`, with no create and no truncate, before `write_atomic`. Any error other than `NotFound` is refused with the "is read-only" message. `crates/app/src/project/wire.rs:334-339`.
- This closes the blocker. On Unix, a file owned by another user with mode `0644` gives `EACCES` from that open, so the save refuses and the rename never replaces the file. I checked this on this machine: a `0644` file owned by uid 65534 in a `0775` folder owned by the saving user gave `EACCES` on `O_WRONLY`, and the file content did not change. `NotFound` is allowed, so a new project path still works.
- The probe holds no handle over the rename. `is_err_and` consumes the `Result` and drops the `File` before `write_atomic` runs, so a Windows rename is not blocked by an open target.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` enters the non-test code. The probe uses `is_err_and` and builds an `Error` by name.
- The temp-file and rename paths are unchanged by this commit, and they still free the temp file on error (`crates/app/src/machine/store.rs:130-149`, the `remove_file` at `:144`). The closure that runs `File::create`, `write_all`, `sync_all` and `rename` removes the temp on any error.
- The delta adds two tests, and the decision doc records the write-open rule for the shared-folder case (`docs/decisions/3509-atomic-project-save.md`).

## Results merged with main (locally, this machine)

Trial merge = main `64b737729` + head `eab5f1932`, clean. `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=3`, no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, no sccache.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `project_roundtrip` suite | ok, 82 passed, 0 failed |
| `machine_edit` suite | ok, 13 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean, exit 0 |

Each pinning test alone with `--exact`:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `a_project_save_replaces_the_file_and_leaves_no_temp_file` | ok |
| `a_failed_project_save_keeps_the_old_file` | ok |
| `a_project_save_into_a_missing_folder_is_refused_and_makes_no_folder` | ok |
| `a_read_only_project_file_is_refused_and_kept` | ok |
| `a_project_save_over_a_unix_socket_is_refused_and_kept` | ok |
| `a_project_save_into_a_folder_without_write_access_is_refused_and_kept` | ok |
| `two_threads_never_share_a_temp_file` | ok |

The socket test is red before the probe: a socket has mode `0775`, so `readonly()` is false, and I confirmed that a rename replaces a socket in a writable folder. The probe is the check that refuses it. The cross-user case needs another uid to pin; the commit message says so, and I checked it by hand above.

## Heavy lanes

Heavy not run - owed to the cut. This is a project-save fix and not the safety floor, so the #3558 standard gives no targeted heavy step. A PR comment records a maintainer-side heavy run on `dbe37ad2c`: 207 steps, 0 failed. The same comment says a run on `eab5f1932` is in progress.

## Requested before merge

No blockers.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- The PR body still says `Effort: low`. Issue #3509 carries `effort:high`, and the safety floor puts saving work at high. The body line should match or be dropped.
- `crates/app/tests/project_roundtrip.rs` is now 5620 lines, already over the 400-line rule. This commit adds 46 lines. A later split along a domain seam would help.
- The two new tests are `#[cfg(unix)]`. On Windows the read-only-attribute case stays covered by the `Permissions::readonly()` check, but the new write-probe path has no Windows assertion.
- The PR is still a draft. The maintainer flags it ready right before the merge (Pull Request Law).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
